notes: Summary: Mid-market B2B SaaS (HelpDeskly) building internal IT/helpdesk chatbot to reduce L1 tickets. Evaluating Redwood Hosted API first to move quickly, then likely Dedicated for isolation and predictable SLAs.
Business drivers: reduce agent handling time, faster mean time to resolution for internal IT, better auditability for compliance and HR/privacy requests.

Technical priorities: streaming partial responses for perceived latency, tool-calling to create/update Jira tickets and fetch KB articles, sub-300-350ms first-byte target for standard queries, ability to burst to ~500 concurrent chats during peak.
Security/Compliance: SAML SSO required for internal users, audit logs for all chat sessions, 12-month retention on transcripts (may extend), KMS for key management, US data residency preferred.

POC notes: running on Hosted API seeded with internal KB and tool-call hooks. Instrumented latency tracing required (per-route/token-level breakdown). Team wants an explicit fallback plan: if hosted can't meet 99.9% latency SLO, move to Dedicated with reserved capacity.
Cost sensitivity: mid-market budget - wants unit economics examples and a pricing cadence showing hosted per-token vs committed capacity on Dedicated.
Quotes: 'We need the bot to feel instant — partial tokens streaming is a must, otherwise users hang.' — Head of Product.
Integration: currently use AWS (us-east-1), Jira Cloud, Confluence; want examples of tool-calling patterns and security model for backend integrations.
Internal stakeholders: Head of Product (Natalie Chen), Director of Engineering (Marco Alvarez), IT Ops Manager (Priya Nair), Security Lead (Ethan Cole).
Decision criteria: latency (SLO + p95), security posture (SOC2, audit logs), predictable cost, ease of integration with existing ticketing stack.

Next steps (from AE): run latency-focused POC, provide perf report + recommended Dedicated sizing, share pricing scenarios (hosted vs reserved Dedicated), arrange security call to review SOC2 and KMS options.
